name: System Fighter
sublight: very high thrust, flies in atmosphere
desc: Single-seat dogfighter. Space is an ocean and this is a Spitfire — banks, stalls, and turns like an aeroplane because the setting wants it to. Hyperdrive for the jump between scenes.

name: Light Freighter
desc: The scoundrel's ship — small hold, oversized engines, a gun turret, and a hyperdrive that's always one bad roll from failing. The party's home.

name: Capital Dreadnought
desc: Kilometre-scale wedge bristling with batteries and fighter bays. Uses Damage Scale wholesale — a setpiece, not a stat line you dogfight.

name: Exploration Cruiser
desc: A flying town: labs, families, a captain who talks first. FTL is a *cruise speed*, not a jump, so travel time is a plot dial the GM turns.

name: Shuttle / Runabout
desc: The away-team car — atmosphere-capable, modest warp, the vehicle that actually gets characters to the surface.

name: Gate Portal
desc: Not a ship — a doorway. You can only go where a gate already stands, which makes the *map of gates* the campaign map. Stargate-style FTL.

name: Torch Freighter
desc: Hard-SF hauler à la ForeSight's own physics (and The Expanse): you burn toward your target, flip at the midpoint, and burn to stop. No FTL — the solar system *is* the setting.

name: Corvette (Torch)
desc: Newtonian warship: no shields, no banking — just delta-v, point-defence, and the tyranny of the rocket equation. Combat is about vectors and reaction mass.

name: Mass-Shunt Tug
desc: ForeSight's original FTL: the *mass shunt* throws a ship between fixed points (a magic gate serves the same role in a fantasy-SF setting). Torch drive does everything in-system; the shunt links the stars.

name: General Systems Vehicle
desc: A sentient Mind wearing a ship the size of a country, home to millions and able to build more of itself. Post-scarcity: 'stats' are whatever the Mind decides. The setting where the ship is the most powerful *character*.

name: Fast Picket
desc: A small, appallingly fast, appallingly armed Mind. Diplomacy-by-presence; when one arrives, the scene is already over. Effectors and gridfire sit far off any mundane Damage Scale.

name: Effector Drone
desc: A sentient, fist-to-suitcase-sized machine — companion, bodyguard, and party member. The Culture's answer to 'what does a PC-scale piece of tech look like when it's also a person?'
